newsitem.title: UK: More EU sugar licences likely if storage refund cut.
newsitem.headline: More EU sugar licences likely if storage refund cut.

text.p: The European Commission's proposal to reduce the 1997/98 sugar storage refund could prompt more bids at its weekly export licence tenders as storage costs increase, analysts said on Thursday.
On Wednesday, the Commission proposed to cut the monthly storage refund by 17 percent to 0.35 Ecus per 100 kg, with sources saying the planned reduction took account of lower interest rates.
Analysts said such a reduction in the storage refund, applicable to uncleared A and B quota sugars, would have to be accompanied by a similar cut in the initial storage levy paid by producers.
"The whole point of the storage rebate is to pay either the producer or the traders the cost of finance and warehouse rents," said an analyst at a major London-based trade house.
"Unless there's a commensurate cut in the levy then it's a little bit one-sided. It means that it isn't so clever to store uncleared AB sugar," he said.
Given the extra costs involved in storing their sugar, producers might opt to export rather than pay warehouse fees that would either be stable or rise with inflation.
If this were the case, more bids could be seen at the Commission's weekly tenders for export licences, he said.
"It won't affect the restitution but it might be that there are more licences granted as people are forced to move the AB sugar as opposed to C," he said.
Analysts said the Commission's storage refund payments were probably starting to mount up as ex-warehouse movements had recently seen more C sugar than either A or B.
On March 17/18, European Commission Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler will present the farm price proposals to farm ministers, who are due to take a decision by the end of June.
